questions.prompt: Explain how leave decisions are authorized and why the leave workflow is modeled as explicit states.

keyPoints.text: A role is only part of authorization; the server combines verified identity with the current reporting relationship.
keyPoints.quote: The server combines verified identity with the current reporting relationship.

keyPoints.text: A manager cannot decide every employee's leave, only their direct reports'.
HR can review leave organization-wide but still cannot approve their own request.
keyPoints.quote: yet still cannot approve their own request

keyPoints.text: The UI shows appropriate controls, while the API enforces the same rules independently.
keyPoints.quote: the API independently enforces the same rules

keyPoints.text: Accepted decisions are not overwritten with arbitrary status strings.
keyPoints.quote: Accepted decisions are not overwritten with arbitrary status strings.

keyPoints.text: Cancellation keeps the previous decision information and adds its own audit event, unlike deletion of a pending record.
keyPoints.quote: Cancellation retains the previous decision information and adds its own audit event.

keyPoints.text: decide checks self-approval, then HR or current direct manager.

questions.prompt: Explain how overlapping leave is prevented, including what each of the two protection layers contributes.

keyPoints.text: Dates are calendar days, accepted as canonical YYYY-MM-DD values and stored as date columns.
keyPoints.quote: Dates are calendar days, not arbitrary timestamps.

keyPoints.text: Intervals are inclusive: a request from the 10th to the 12th includes the 12th.
keyPoints.quote: A request from July 10 through July 12 includes July 12

keyPoints.text: The application locks the employee row while checking and writing an active interval, so cooperating requests serialize.
keyPoints.quote: Cooperating requests for the same employee therefore serialize.

keyPoints.text: A PostgreSQL exclusion constraint independently rejects overlapping pending or approved intervals, even from writers that bypass the repository.
keyPoints.quote: including writes that bypass repository validation

keyPoints.text: The application layer is overlap() in the leave repository: inside the caller's transaction it runs a findFirst for a pending or approved request whose dates intersect and answers a hit with an AppError 409.
The constraint is declared in the migration with an inclusive daterange.

questions.prompt: Explain versions, transactions and the chart lock: what each guarantees and what the single constant lock costs.

keyPoints.text: A request loaded at version one must send version one even if another tab saved version two.
keyPoints.quote: must send expected version one, even if another tab has since saved version two

keyPoints.text: Attaching the latest version to an old draft would bypass that protection.
keyPoints.quote: Fetching the latest version and attaching it to an old draft would bypass that protection.

keyPoints.text: Transactions group the entity change with its audit, so a failed audit rolls the mutation back.
keyPoints.quote: If audit insertion fails, the mutation rolls back.

keyPoints.text: Reporting cycles are forbidden, and an advisory lock stops two plausible concurrent changes from forming one together.
keyPoints.quote: preventing two individually plausible concurrent changes from creating a cycle together

keyPoints.text: The single constant lock means every employee write in the system waits for every other.
A per-chain key would allow parallel edits, but joining two chains then needs both roots locked in a fixed order.
keyPoints.quote: you must lock both roots in a fixed order or you trade the cycle bug for a deadlock

keyPoints.text: chartLock is one pg_advisory_xact_lock with a constant key.
